transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
Thanks for seeing me. I’ve felt this heavy, low mood every day for over a year, like I just can’t shake feeling down no matter what I do.
Can you tell me more about how long you've been experiencing this low mood, and has it been consistently present for the entire year or have you had any periods where your mood improved?

It's been going on steadily for a little over a year now, starting shortly after my wife moved out with our son. This heavy feeling hasn't lifted or improved at all during this time, even when I'm spending time with my son or when something good happens at work.

You mentioned that even good things at work or spending time with your son don't improve your mood; do you still find pleasure in activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy before your wife and son moved out?

No, I don't enjoy any of it anymore. I used to love organizing pickup basketball, volunteering, and grilling with friends on weekends, but now even the thought of doing those things feels completely exhausting and pointless. I just make excuses to stay home and sit on the couch flipping through channels without caring about any of it.

Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since you started feeling this low mood, such as eating more or less than usual, or sleeping more or less than you used to?

Yes, both have been terrible. I lie awake staring at the ceiling for hours and wake up around 3 AM with my mind racing, and my appetite is completely gone. I've skipped so many meals that I've lost a lot of weight, and my coworkers have even commented on how gaunt I look.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless, and if so, are these feelings connected to your current situation or more about yourself in general?

I feel incredibly guilty all the time, constantly telling myself that I'm a terrible husband and father who ruined his family by being selfish and absent. I just replay every argument with my wife in my head over and over, and I've become convinced they would all be better off without me screwing things up.
Have you experienced episodes of depression like this before in your life, or is this the first time you've felt this persistent low mood?
No, this is the first time I've ever experienced anything like this. I've never had any history of depression or felt this kind of persistent low mood before these difficulties started a year ago.

Given that you've had this persistent low mood for over a year without any improvement, can you tell me if you've had any periods, even brief, where you felt somewhat better or if the severity of your symptoms has varied at all over this time?

No, there really haven't been any periods where I felt better. This heavy, numb feeling has been completely constant and steady for over a year now. It just doesn't lift, even when I'm spending time with my son or when something good happens at work.

You've mentioned that your low mood has been constant for over a year without any improvement, but can you think of any specific events, days, or moments where your mood might have slightly improved, even if just for a short while, or has it been unrelenting the entire time?

No, it has been completely unrelenting, without even a brief moment of relief. Even during times that should be positive—like spending time with my son or when something goes well at work—that heavy, hollow feeling and numbness in my chest just stay there. It leaves me constantly feeling like there's just no point.

You've described a persistent low mood for over a year without any improvement, which is helpful. To clarify, have you experienced any periods of at least two months where you felt significantly better, or has the low mood been consistently present the entire time?
No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all, let alone for two months. This heavy, numb feeling has been consistently present every single day since my wife left with our son.
Have you ever had a period of significant improvement in your mood that lasted for at least two weeks, or has your mood remained consistently low since your wife and son moved out?

No, I haven't had even a two-week break where I felt like my old self or felt any lift in my mood. It has just been a steady, daily struggle with this heavy feeling for over a year now since they left.

Can you confirm if you've had any episodes of significant mood elevation or irritability, even if brief, alongside your persistent low mood, or has your mood been solely and consistently low without any periods of elevated mood?
No, I haven't had any periods of elevated mood, high energy, or "highs" at all. It has been solely and consistently low, just that same heavy, numb feeling every single day.

You've described your mood as consistently low without any periods of improvement, but can you tell me if there have been any subtle variations in the intensity of your low mood, even if it's just a matter of feeling slightly less bad on some days compared to others?

No, there really aren't any lighter days or variations. From the moment I wake up until I go to sleep, that heavy, hollow feeling in my chest remains completely constant. It doesn't lift at all, even during potentially positive moments like spending time with my son or when something good happens at work.

You've mentioned that your low mood has been constant and unrelenting, but can you think of any situations or events, no matter how small, that might have caused a slight, even temporary, change in the intensity of your low mood, such as feeling slightly more or less down in response to something specific?

Positive things like being with my son or doing well at work don't lift my mood at all. But the feeling definitely gets much heavier and more intense late at night when I'm alone in the empty house and can't sleep. I just lie there replaying the arguments with my wife and thinking that everyone would be better off without me.

Can you clarify if you've experienced any periods where your low mood significantly worsened or improved in response to specific events or stressors, or has it remained constant regardless of what's happening in your life?

It has remained constant regardless of what is happening in my life. It first developed after my wife moved out with our son, but since then, it has just been a steady, heavy presence that doesn't lift, even during good moments.

Have you experienced any periods of at least two weeks where your symptoms significantly improved, allowing you to function more normally, or has your low mood been consistently present without any notable breaks?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that at all. This heavy, depressed feeling has been going on steadily every single day for over a year now. There hasn't been any period, let alone two weeks, where I felt like my normal self or experienced any real relief.
Can you confirm whether you have experienced any episode of depression that lasted for more than two years, or if this current episode is the longest you've experienced so far?

I've never experienced anything like this before this past year, so I don't have any prior episodes to compare it to. This current year-long period is the first and longest time I've ever felt this way.

Given that you've had this persistent low mood for over a year without any prior episodes, can you tell me if you believe this current episode of depression might be related to the specific life event of your wife and son moving out, or do you think there might be other underlying factors contributing to your condition?

Yes, it definitely started when my wife and son moved out to her sister's house after months of strain over my heavy work travel. Once they left, things completely spiraled and this heavy cloud settled over me. Being left alone in that empty house just made me feel like an absolute failure who ruined his family.

Do you believe that if your family situation were to improve, such as your wife and son returning, your low mood would significantly lift, or do you feel that your depression has become more of an independent issue regardless of your family's situation?

While losing my family is definitely the root of all my guilt and pain, this depression now feels like its own heavy, independent constant. Even when I get to see my son, that hollow feeling doesn't lift at all. It just feels like I can't shake this mood anymore, regardless of what happens.
Have you had any previous episodes of depression that were shorter than two years, or is this the first episode you've experienced?
This is the very first time I've ever experienced anything like this. I have no prior history of depression at all, so I've never had any shorter episodes in the past.

You've mentioned this is your first episode of depression, lasting over a year. Can you understand why distinguishing between a single episode of depression versus recurrent episodes is important for your diagnosis and treatment?

To be honest, as a sales manager, I don't really know the clinical reasons behind distinguishing between a single episode and recurrent ones. But I'm definitely open to hearing you explain it if you think it would help with my treatment.

Can you understand that your diagnosis might be either a single episode of major depressive disorder or recurrent depressive disorder, and that understanding the duration and potential recurrence of your symptoms will help guide the treatment approach?

That makes sense, and I appreciate you explaining it to me. This is the very first time I've ever felt this way or sought help, and it's been constant and steady for a little over a year now since my wife left with my son. I'm just tired of feeling like this and want to do whatever we need to do to get some help.

Are you aware of any factors or patterns that might suggest this episode of depression could recur in the future, or do you believe this is an isolated response to the specific life event of your family leaving?

I've never experienced anything like this before in my life, so it feels entirely tied to my family leaving. To me, this depression feels like a direct consequence of my marriage falling apart and the guilt I carry for ruining our lives. It doesn't feel like some recurring pattern from my past, just the heavy reality of what I've done to my family.

Given that this is your first episode of depression and it's been over a year, do you think that if you were to experience significant improvement or remission of your symptoms, you would be at risk of having another episode of depression in the future?

To be honest, I haven't really thought about the future or the risk of having another episode down the road. Right now, it's hard enough just trying to get through each day with how heavy everything feels. I'm just completely focused on trying to survive this present struggle.

If your symptoms were to significantly improve with treatment, do you think the underlying issues related to your family situation and personal guilt would still pose a risk for triggering another depressive episode in the future?

I'm really not sure what the future holds. Right now, the guilt and my family situation feel so heavy and overwhelming that it's hard to even imagine how things will look if this depression gets better. Because of that, I honestly don't know if those same issues would just trigger it all over again down the road.

Given your symptoms have been constant for over a year without any prior episodes, do you believe that resolving your current life stressors, such as reconnecting with your family, would potentially lead to a full remission of your depressive symptoms, or do you think your depression has taken on a life of its own?

I'm really not sure because everything feels so heavy and dark right now that it's hard to imagine things ever getting better. Even if my family came back, this cloud has settled in so deeply that I don't know if it would just go away.

Considering your symptoms have been constant for over a year and this is your first episode of depression, do you think that if your current symptoms were to improve, you would still be at risk of experiencing another episode of depression in the future due to your past experiences and stressors?

I haven't really thought about the risk of another episode or what might happen in the future. Right now, I'm just so overwhelmed trying to get through each day that I can't even imagine what lies down the road. I feel too hopeless to think about anything past just getting through today.
Do you think the issues related to your family situation and personal guilt could potentially trigger another depressive episode in the future, even if your current symptoms improve with treatment?

I really haven't thought about the future or what might trigger another episode. Right now, I'm just so overwhelmed by my present guilt and this heavy depression that I can't even imagine getting better, let alone looking ahead.

Given that you've had no prior episodes of depression and this is your first episode lasting over a year, do you think that the current episode might be a single, prolonged response to the stress of your family leaving, or could it be the start of a pattern of recurrent depressive episodes?

I'm really not sure because I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. While these feelings definitely started and got worse after my wife and son left, I don't know if this is just a prolonged reaction to that specific stress or the beginning of a recurring pattern.

Do you think that if your current depressive symptoms were to significantly improve, you would still experience episodes of depression in the future, or do you believe this is an isolated episode related to your current life circumstances?

I'm really not sure, and I haven't thought about the future at all. Right now, I'm just too overwhelmed by my marriage problems and this heavy feeling to even think about what might happen down the road.

Do you think that if your family situation were to significantly improve, such as your wife and son returning, you would still experience depressive episodes in the future, or do you believe your depression would fully remit?

I honestly don't know. It's so hard for me to even imagine the future or what it would feel like if they came back. Right now, I'm just too stuck in this heavy feeling to know if it would ever fully go away.
